title: Lior and the Safehouse
premise: Sebastian Coldharbour, an air-crash investigator haunted by the death of his family in row twelve, is approached by a woman claiming he once sheltered her from a trafficking network he doesn't remember helping — a debt incurred during the missing weeks he can't account for. As she calls in the favor, Sebastian uncovers that the 'safehouse' network that once trained and erased him is now liquidating its assets, including him. Racing through a sleepless week to Frankfurt, he must expose and burn the network's financial core before the markets open, trading his last chance at anonymity — and a fragile new life with the woman he saved — for the truth of what he did to survive.
about_author: Dominic Okonkwo is a former logistics auditor from Lagos who writes thrillers about systems that consume the people who run them. He lives between Lisbon and Accra, where he collects timetables from airlines that no longer exist.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A sleepless night of crash-report drafts and insomnia rituals is interrupted by a knock: a woman named Ilsa returns a key he supposedly gave her, saying 'the favor is called in.' Emotional beat: the first crack in his carefully maintained numbness — someone knows he existed before the grief.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He investigates Ilsa's story and finds physical evidence — his handwriting, his old codes — from weeks he cannot remember, including a gap in his own employment file. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession; the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She reveals the network: handlers, safehouses, and a training program that manufactures 'invisible' operatives, then erases them. She believes Sebastian was one of them. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, two survivors comparing scars neither can fully see.

chapters.title: Liquidation Notice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A former handler turns up dead in a manner matching Sebastian's own training signature, and an encrypted notice lists 'Coldharbour, S.' among assets to be written down. Emotional beat: the hunter's cold clarity returning — he has until Friday, when the network's holding company settles in Frankfurt.

chapters.title: What the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Under pressure, Sebastian's erased skills surface — dead drops, counter-surveillance, a fluency in violence that horrifies him. A flashback surfaces: row twelve was not an accident he investigated; it was one he was meant to cause. Emotional beat: self-loathing as the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Frankfurt Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the money, they find the network's true product: not operatives, but insurable catastrophes — crashes, collapses, 'accidents' sold short before they happen. Row twelve was a trade. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the insomnia becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The network's cleaner, a man Ilsa once trusted, corners them; Sebastian's buried training saves them both, but he crosses a line he can't come back from. Ilsa admits her favor was a recruitment gambit — she needed him angry enough to act. Emotional beat: betrayal inside trust, and forgiveness offered anyway.

chapters.title: Night Before the Open
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They assemble the evidence: ledgers, flight manifests, the trade that killed his family. Sebastian sleeps for the first time in years — two hours, dreamless — and wakes ready. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm; inheritance of his own past, chosen this time.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Ilsa's alternating POV. At the Frankfurt exchange, they inject the ledger into the network's own settlement systems as the markets open, triggering a cascade that freezes the assets and exposes the principals mid-trade. The cleaner makes a last attempt; Sebastian chooses arrest over killing. Emotional beat: climax — burning the network without becoming it.

chapters.title: The Long Sleep
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Weeks later: hearings, testimony, a settlement that can't restore row twelve but names it. Ilsa leaves a key and an open door. Sebastian sleeps through the night and wakes to morning light. Emotional beat: resolution — survival's price paid, memory kept, and the first honest rest.
